Res. 74)
bill.status: Introduced in Senate · Whitehouse · referred to Commerce, Science, and Transportation

provisions.title: S.J. Res. 74
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the PHMSA rule at 90 Fed. Reg. 21434
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration relating to Pipeline Safety: Editorial Change To Reflect the Name Change of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America (90 Fed. Reg. 21434 (May 20, 2025)), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
S.J. Res. 74 is an introduced Senate joint resolution under chapter 8 of title 5. Its single operative clause disapproves the PHMSA rule identified by title and Federal Register citation and states that the rule shall have no force or effect. That legal consequence is contingent on enactment; introduction and referral alone do not make the rule ineffective. The resolution supplies no replacement regulatory wording, implementation timetable, appropriation, reporting duty, substantive pipeline-safety standard, or quantitative target.

Source limits / honesty note: The supplied flattened text identifies but does not reproduce the cited rule, the affected regulatory text, or chapter 8, and it includes no findings, purpose section, or sponsor rationale. The matching official PDF establishes pagination at two pages, but the flat extraction omits page boundaries and the standard resolving formula. This extraction therefore does not infer which terminology would apply after disapproval, any government-wide effect on the geographic name, or changes to safety, compliance costs, or agency workload. It identifies zero forecastable recurring official metrics, zero defensible series hints, and zero empirical conditional forecasts; the observable legal status is categorical, and a conditional on enactment would merely restate the clause.
goals: Make the PHMSA rule cited at 90 Fed. Reg. 21434 have no force or effect through congressional disapproval.

effects.text: If the joint resolution is enacted, the cited rule would have no force or effect; the text does not itself prescribe replacement wording or alter a substantive pipeline-safety standard.
